title: Hard cores hold off the wall within the Quiver's reach; the strip names the mounts; every mount sights from its perch
context: Owner could not get the Quiver lock to work by hand: while the lock is tuned, make the hard enemies stop and move around outside the base, within range but not too close; and make it possible to select which tower to manual-override.
outcome: story-world builds a holding ring of lane cells hold[0]..hold[1] hops outside the forward cell; in the enemy step a story hard core inside the ring only wanders within it; the Quiver override triggers at nearCells (5) from the gate. The strip renders TANK, one button per printed mount (from the towers' labels), MAP; a mount button enters that optic or picks it via a new pilot host `pick` while already piloting. The acceptance's reach dump then showed both hard cores within 27 m of the Quiver with no line of sight: losClear sampled from the rock's centre, so a ray down the lane grazed the next ridge cell. losClear now takes an origin and every mount site passes its perch (auto hitscan, pilot visibility, aim and reach hooks). Controller 17,609 lines, budget lowered.
alternatives: Bias the lock toward hard cores: not the problem, the optic never saw them.
Raise the platform: would not have changed a ground-level cell-sampled ray.
evidence: browser --story-world PASS: hard cores at 19 and 26 m in the ring, two kills from two rounds, ROTOR and QUIVER buttons pick their optic; --dist legacy PASS
